subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Carbon Capture: Engineering the Air Clean
description: One-minute skill: Carbon Capture: Engineering the Air Clean.

hook.text: Direct air capture machines suck CO2 from the atmosphere. Climeworks' Orca plant in Iceland captures 4,000 tons per year.

buildup.text: Fans draw air over chemical filters that bind CO2. The filters are heated to release pure CO2, which is then stored underground.

discovery.text: CO2 makes up only 0.04% of the atmosphere. Extracting it is like finding a needle in a haystack — energy-intensive and expensive.

twist.text: Humanity emits 37 billion tons of CO2 annually. Orca captures 4,000 tons. Current capacity is millions of times too small.

climax.text: Climeworks' Mammoth plant, opening in 2024, is ten times larger. Costs must drop from $600 to under $100 per ton to scale up.

punchline.text: Suck it from the air. Bury it underground. The scale is the problem.

quiz.question: Why is direct air capture currently impractical at the scale needed?
options: The chemical filters used to capture CO2 are made from rare earth minerals
Costs are around $600 per ton and humanity emits 37 billion tons annually
Captured CO2 cannot be stored safely underground for more than a few years
